# UFO

## Slice-of-life vignette set in a rural environment.

- "Do you like feesh?" asked Maria, her voice carrying a distinct Eastern European accent.

- "Fish?" — Robert asked. "I like the taste of its flesh," he replied, picking thin bones stuck between his teeth. He
needed to make sure he was understood correctly.

Two figures were sitting in the outdoor kitchen.

A mesh hung on the doorway to keep flies out. Even after most of them had been chased outside, two flies still
remained, flying in loops. This pair of flies periodically landed on the edge of the table, crawling closer to the
board where the fish was laid out, which Robert was methodically consuming.

The conversation was about a UFO that someone supposedly saw nearby.

The clamor of roosters and geese emanated from the yard outside.

- "You ever see UFO?" — Maria asked, chewing on bread, moving closer to Robert.

- "Seen?" — Robert repeated. "I look at sky carefully every evening. Honestly, I believe I saw unidentified flying
object," he said, emphasizing every word so Maria would understand him correctly.

Maria liked how Robert expressed his thoughts. She smiled, her voice soft and colorful.

- "And vot it look like?" she continued with interest.

- "It was round, glowing spot," Robert replied, squinting his eyes. "I'm sure it wasn't plane or star."

Maria leaned forward, listening intently.

- "And can you say exactly vere you saw it?"

- "Of course," — Robert wiped his lips, slightly leaning his palms on the edges of the table, lifting his fingers and
looking somewhere to the side, remembering. "It was in the west, right above the forest. I'm sure of it because I watch
sunset from that spot every evening."

Maria nodded, looking at him thoughtfully.

- "I hear many people saw something similar in those parts," she said, adjusting her dress. "You not first."

Robert nodded, continuing to explain his observations, trying to be as precise as possible so Maria would understand
the accuracy of his words. She listened to him with admiration. The conversation about the sunset, the forest, the
unidentified flying object in their area — all of this added a special warmth, coziness, and soul-tickling depth of
mystery to the conversation, especially since not much usually happened around their place.

- "You know, Robert, you notice everysing so precise," she said with a smile. "I like how you tell it. Everysing is so clear and clearly."

Robert smiled in return, pleased that his words were understood.
